corrections.old: Tim Richard, an e-commerce founder, lists nine 'boring' product niches that he says have high Google search volume, low keyword difficulty and few dedicated brands. They are stainless steel litter boxes, hojicha latte, satin sheets, rice water shampoo, key fob covers, beef protein powder, men's crossbody bags, non-tarnish jewelry and floor couches. His method is to use social media and Ahrefs keyword data to find rising search trends, then build a branded site around one specific term. The picks are his own opinion, with no tested sales data for any of them. The video also promotes his paid 'idea book' database.

notes: Overall the extraction is solid: all nine listicle products are captured, plus the Antler ring example, and the deconstructions, scores and C rating are reasonable. The main problem is the invented host name 'Tim Richard', which also appears in every speaker and claimant field; it should be replaced with 'Host'. Several per-product search-volume claims were missed and are added here. A few small unsupported details were corrected: the idea book being 'paid' and the cheap-ads inference for litter boxes. The $15k first-month claim is ambiguous: it is unclear whether it refers to one of the nine products or to one of the host's own products.
